verses.text: Watch your step when you go to God's house. It's better to come close and listen than to offer a sacrifice like fools who don't even know they're doing wrong.
Don't speak before you think, and don't rush to say whatever's on your heart before God. God is in heaven, and you're on earth. So keep your words few.
Just as many worries bring on dreams, many words bring out a fool's speech.
When you make a promise to God, don't put off keeping it. He takes no pleasure in fools. Do what you promised.
It's better to make no promise than to make one and fail to keep it.
Don't let your mouth lead you into sin. Don't tell the messenger it was a mistake. Why give God reason to be angry at what you said and tear down what you've worked for?
There's emptiness in piles of dreams and piles of words. Fear God.
If you see the poor oppressed and justice and righteousness ripped away in a district, don't be surprised. A higher official watches each official, and there are officials above them too.
The land yields something for everyone. Even the king benefits from the fields.
Anyone who loves money never gets enough money. Anyone who loves having plenty never gets enough of the gains. This too is empty.
When goods pile up, more people come to consume them. What's left for the owner to enjoy except the sight of it all?
A worker sleeps sweetly, whether they ate a little or a lot. But the wealth of the rich keeps them awake.
I've seen a painful evil under the sun. Someone holds on to wealth and ends up harmed by it.
Then misfortune wipes out those riches. If that person has a son, there's nothing left to put in his hands.
They came naked from their mother's womb and will leave just as naked. They can't carry away a thing from all their work.
This too is a painful evil. A person leaves exactly as they came. What do they gain from working for the wind?
They eat in darkness all their days, worn down by frustration, sickness, and anger.
Here's what I've seen is good and fitting. Eat, drink, and enjoy the good in all your work under the sun during the days God gives you. That's your share.
When God gives someone wealth and possessions and lets them enjoy them, accept their share, and find joy in their work, that's God's gift.
They won't spend much time dwelling on the days of their life, because God keeps their heart busy with joy.
